title: This Newly Discovered Dinosaur Looks Terrifying—But Probably Wouldn’t Eat You - Nautilus
gist: Chinese and U.S. paleontologists describe Kayrasaurus changliensis, a nearly complete therizinosaur from China's Yixian Formation that is almost twice as large as previous therizinosaurs there — over 11.8 feet long and up to 604 pounds — despite likely being a juvenile.

insights.claim: Therizinosaurs were bipedal dinosaurs with small beaked heads on long necks, feathers and some of the longest claws ever found in nature.
insights.speaker: David Nield

insights.claim: Kayrasaurus changliensis is almost twice as big as previous therizinosaurs found at the Yixian Formation in northeastern China, and paleontologists have nearly its entire skeleton.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Highlights China's Yixian Formation as a productive fossil site; no market signal.

insights.claim: Researchers estimate K. changliensis was more than 11.8 feet long, taller than a grizzly bear on its hind legs, and weighed up to 604 pounds.
insights.speaker: David Nield

insights.claim: The Chinese and U.S. researchers believe the K. changliensis skeleton is a juvenile, so the species likely grew larger than these estimates.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Example of continuing China–U.S. scientific collaboration in paleontology.
insights.quote: presumably this wasn’t the species’ peak size

insights.claim: Despite its terrifying appearance, Kayrasaurus changliensis probably would not have eaten humans.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.locator: This Newly Discovered Dinosaur Looks Terrifying
